guidelineReference: Resus Council UK Acute Coronary Syndromes 2021
title: Suspected heart attack at a football match
setting: Football stands. 60M spectator has severe chest pain, lightheaded, known history of angina. Carries GTN spray.
verdictExplanation: Chest pain with radiation to the arm, shortness of breath, and risk of myocardial infarction in a patient with active angina. Sick: administer GTN and monitor closely.

shared.danger: Stairs and crowds in football stands
shared.circulation: Fast pulse, skin is pale, cold, and clammy

history.history: Felt okay when arrived, developed chest discomfort radiating to left arm in the last 30 minutes

followUp.question: Which of the following clinical findings most strongly suggests that this is an acute myocardial infarction (heart attack) rather than an episode of stable angina?

options.text: The severity of the pain (9/10) persisting for 30 minutes at rest, combined with pale, clammy skin and low oxygen saturation (90%)
The fact that he carries a GTN spray in his coat pocket
His blood pressure of 124/90 mmHg, which confirms cardiogenic shock

followUp.explanation: Stable angina typically resolves within minutes of rest or GTN use. A severe, radiating 9/10 chest pain persisting for 30 minutes at rest, combined with hypoxia, tachycardia, and clammy skin, strongly points to an acute myocardial infarction.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Place in W-position, call 999 immediately for a suspected heart attack. Assist with GTN and chewable aspirin.
levelFlags.erNotes: ACS protocol. Administer oxygen if SpO₂ <94%, give aspirin 300mg chewable if not already taken. Monitor BP and prepare AED in case of arrest.
